move: phone rises, sleep stacks build bottom to top, counters tick, collapse
how: Portrait 1080x1920: a dark phone frame with notch rises from y:80/opacity:0 (power3.out) over the first 16%; the header, hero time readout and delta slide up y:24 with stagger 0.1. Two gridlines scale in scaleX from the left (expo.out), day letters fade in. From 16% each of seven days builds its stack: the deep segment grows scaleY from 0 at the baseline (expo.out, 0.6s), then core 0.1s later and REM 0.2s later, each starting translated down by the height of the segments beneath it (y from a function reading offsetHeight) so the stack appears to extrude upward; days are staggered 0.12. An object tween from 18% to 50% counts hours/minutes, deep-sleep percent and score (power2.out); legend chips and two stat cards slide in. At 56% today's bar breathes scaleY 1.03 yoyo. Exit at 83%: all segments collapse scaleY to 0 with expo.in staggered from the end, then the phone lifts out y:-60.
adapt: Edit the days array (letter, deep, core, rem hours) and the three segment colours in .seg.deep/.core/.rem and the legend --c values; set the hero numbers in the counter tween (h, m, p, s); keep the 0.1s segment cascade and 0.12 day stagger. Layout is portrait, change the phone size for 16:9.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone and generates .day stacks from shot.days; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with stack builds at 0.16-0.4 of D and collapse at 0.83. The y function values read offsetHeight and must be evaluated after layout (GSAP function-based values do this at tween creation, so build the timeline after mount is laid out). getElementById calls scoped to el.
caveats: segment offsets are function-based values read from offsetHeight at build time, so fonts and layout must be settled
phone enters from below and exits upward, no loop
